Based on the provided authoritative legal context for Financial Year 2023-24 (Assessment Year 2024-25), here is the legal analysis regarding the deduction available under Section 80EE:

**1. Maximum Deduction Limit**
The maximum deduction allowable under Section 80EE is **₹50,000** [C2]. This limit is strictly enforced in the e-filing validation rules, where an assessee cannot claim a deduction under Section 80EE exceeding ₹50,000 [C2].

**2. Regime Restriction**
The deduction under Section 80EE is available **only if the "Old Tax Regime" is selected** [C2]. It is not available under the New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC).

**3. Mutual Exclusivity with Section 80EEA**
An assessee cannot claim deductions under both Section 80EE and Section 80EEA simultaneously. The validation rules specify that only one of the deductions under Section 80EE or Section 80EEA is allowed [C5]. Specifically, if the deduction claimed under Section 80EEA is greater than zero, the deduction claimed under Section 80EE cannot be greater than zero [C5].

**4. Eligibility Conditions**
While the specific conditions for "first-time home buyer" status are not detailed in the provided text, the deduction is subject to further conditions specified in sub-section (3) of Section 80EE [C4]. The amount eligible for deduction is the interest paid during the year, subject to the maximum limit of ₹50,000 [C4].

| **Basis** | Interest paid on loan during the year | [C4] |
